meta.title: Ondra Digital Wellbeing
meta.description: Digital wellbeing guardrail for Ondra (L9 extension pool): answers exactly one question — how long has this person been at it continuously, and should something be said right now. The answer is one of four levels (ok / gentle / firm / stop) derived from two non-overlapping readings: the current session (how long this sitting has lasted, broken once the break is long enough) and the daily total (how long today, reset across midnight but not by a break). Merging the two into one number produces two hard-to-diagnose failures: someone who uses eight hours in fragments never hears "that is enough for today", while someone who has sat for three hours straight is treated as having just started. The late-night window is its own signal, and only counts while the person is still active — someone quiet for two hours is probably asleep, and telling them to sleep then is both untrue and alarming. Timing, calendar, day rollover and time zones all come from ondra-clock; this plugin contributes only the threshold judgement and the nudge watermark, falling back to the local time zone when the clock is absent. It never sends messages itself — sending directly bypasses the quiet hours, daily quota, deduplication and risk backoff gates, which exist precisely to prevent eight interruptions a day. It never listens to the keyboard or mouse — global listening requires Accessibility permission on macOS and a guardrail should not quietly ask for it; callers pulse it on real activity instead. It installs no timers — a resident timer is a resident background service, and it keeps counting while nobody watches: leave the machine on overnight and the morning reading claims an eight-hour session. It produces no health score — once there is a "wellbeing score of 62 today", someone will disable the guardrail to protect that number. It renders no UI — rendering belongs to the app shell. It persists timestamps and millisecond totals only: no message text, no window titles, no application names, no screenshots. A wellbeing guardrail that needs to know what you were writing has already overstepped. Level and may-speak-now are kept strictly apart: advise always reports the true level, cooldown only gates nudgeDue, because folding cooldown into the level would hand the shell a fake ok during cooldown while the person has already been sitting for three hours; and "no pulse has ever arrived" is never reported as ok. All three upstreams are soft dependencies — missing clock falls back to the local time zone, missing path keeps state in memory only — and every degradation is visible through stored and the logs.
